why: the per-parameter metadata `rcl_interfaces/msg/ParameterDescriptor` carries -- description, read-only, dynamic typing, range -- as ONE inline value stored beside the parameter. rclrs splits the same information across `ParameterOptions`, `ParameterRanges` and `AvailableValues`, which are owned/`Arc` shaped. Constraint: no allocator -- the descriptor lives in the server's fixed slot array, so the description is a `heapless::String` and the range an inline enum, and both are sized at compile time. `validate_range` is called on every set -- direct `ParameterServer::set`, the typed API, and both `SetParameters` / `SetParametersAtomically` handlers through `ParameterServer::apply` / `check_apply` -- and it enforces min, max AND step (`ParameterRange::contains`, the one predicate for both arms; rclrs `rclrs/src/parameter/range.rs` semantics: either endpoint accepted, off-lattice interior refused, 100-ULP tolerance for doubles), which is where `SetParameterResult::OutOfRange` comes from. Until issue 1150 (fixed 2026-09-06) this sentence was FALSE: `contains()` checked only min/max while `DescribeParameters` published the step. Declare also refuses an ill-formed range (`min > max`, `step < 0`) or a default its own range rejects (`SetParameterResult::InvalidRange`), as upstream. This row covers `ParameterDescriptor::*`. See `rust:ParameterOptions`.
